thread:
cheng: Heads-up — CI perf alert on ROCm images for the latest nightly. p50 token latency jumped ~3.4x on small-batch chat workloads (16 tokens, batch=8). Logs show fallback to generic attention kernel.

maya: Ugh. Any kernel name or signature mismatches in the logs?

cheng: Yep. Runtime prints: `kernel_lookup: no match for signature attention_fused_v3 {wg_size:128, dtype:fp16}` then chooses `attention_generic_v1`.

kevin: That explains it. `attention_generic_v1` has much higher per-token cost for short sequences. Autotuner should have picked a sequence-length path (fused vs generic) but it silently fell back.

rami: Is this an actual missing kernel in the ROCm package or a metadata mismatch? We recently changed how we encode `wg_size` in the kernel manifest.

cheng: Looks like manifest mismatch. The built ROCm kernels still register as `wg_size:0` for some builds. Triage stacktrace attached in CI: `kernel_registry.c:254 kernel_match_failed signature mismatch (expected wg_size>0)`.

perf-bot: perf-alert: nightly/rocm-x86-staging — latency delta +240ms (p50) vs baseline, throughput -45% on chat_small profile.

maya: Two vectors: 1) patch registry parsing so `wg_size:0` is handled as wildcard; 2) add a conditional routing rule to prefer alternate kernel variants on ROCm when manifest mismatch present. Which do we want for a quick mitigation?

kevin: Short term: conditional routing in the policy layer. Prefer `attention_sliced` (available) when fused isn't matched, but only for seq<=64 to avoid quality regressions for long contexts. That avoids shipping a runtime lib change.

cheng: Agreed. We'll push a canary route: if `kernel_match == false && hw_vendor==AMD && seq_len<=64 -> kernel_hint: attention_sliced`. I'll add the policy and a rollout to 5% on dedicated.

rami: FYI, batching heuristics interact here. When we route to `attention_sliced` it expects larger micro-batches; current dynamic batching groups by model+seq and sometimes mixes seq=16 with seq=512 which breaks assumptions. Need to update batching grouping rules for the canary to group strictly by seq bucket.

maya: Good catch. I'll change batching key to include `seq_bucket` for the canary route (buckets: 1-64,65-256,>256). That should keep the microbatch shapes consistent and preserve KV cache locality.

cheng: About KV cache: when we fallback to generic kernel we saw increased cache churn — inferred from the profiler: ``kv_cache_hits: -18%``, likely because the generic kernel uses a different packing layout, invalidating per-request cache entries. Make sure the route doesn't invalidate cache keys.

kevin: We can add a compatibility layer that maps generic kernel layout -> canonical KV key format at runtime. But that's a heavier change. For the canary, ensure `route_metadata.cache_compatible=true` so requests keep the same cache key. Ops will monitor hit-rate.

ops-bot: Canaries: created route `rocm-compat-sliced-v1` -> 5% dedicated. Monitoring: latency/kv_hit_rate/traces enabled.

rami: Longer term we should fix the manifest parser and add an autotune pass that considers sequence-length distributions. Right now autotuner optimizes for average token length and misses short-seq optimized kernels. Add a second objective: minimize p50 for seq<=64.

maya: I'll open the autotuner RFC and a follow-up PR to add signature fuzzing to CI so manifest mismatches fail earlier. Also schedule a kernel package rebuild with correct `wg_size` encoding.

cheng: For tracing: capture `kernel_choice`, `kernel_signature`, `seq_len`, `batch_size`, `kv_key` in spans. That will help quickly detect future mismatches and measure cache compatibility.

kevin: Quick checklist: 
- [ ] Add routing canary (maya)
- [ ] Adjust batching grouping for seq buckets (maya)
- [ ] Patch route_metadata.cache_compatible flag (kevin)
- [ ] Rebuild ROCm kernel package with proper manifests (rami)
- [ ] Autotuner RFC + seq-weighted objective (maya/rami)

rami: I'll queue the package rebuild and add a smoke test that runs the fused attention positive path.

cheng: Thanks. Will watch canary dashboards. If perf stays good we'll rollout to 50% then full. :thumbsup:

kevin: Also note: we should backfill a metric for "kernel_fallback_count" to alert earlier. I'll add an alert threshold at 1% fallback rate for prod.

maya: Created issue #3741 with links to CI logs + perf diffs.

cheng: Closing loop: major root cause = kernel manifest signature mismatch causing autotuner/routing to fallback to slow generic kernels on ROCm. Mitigation = routing canary + batching + cache compatibility flag + package rebuild.

ops-bot: deploy-notes: canary route added 2027-09-02T10:12:05Z.
